definition: to wish that another person does something
example: I want you to connect the bot to the server.
exampleEs: Quiero que conectes el bot al servidor.
cloze: I want you ____ the bot to the server.
note: Spanish uses a subjunctive (quiero que conectes). English uses want + person + to + verb, never 'want that you connect'.

definition: to force or cause someone to do something (no 'to')
example: The bug made me rewrite the whole script.
exampleEs: El error me hizo reescribir todo el script.
cloze: The bug made me ____ the whole script.
note: After make + person, use the bare verb: 'made me rewrite', not 'made me to rewrite'.

definition: to allow someone to do something (no 'to')
example: My manager lets us work from home on Fridays.
exampleEs: Mi jefe nos deja trabajar desde casa los viernes.
cloze: My manager lets us ____ from home on Fridays.
note: Let + person + bare verb. In the passive, use 'be allowed to' instead.

definition: to propose an idea; followed by the -ing form
example: She suggested moving the meeting to Thursday.
exampleEs: Ella sugirió mover la reunión al jueves.
cloze: She suggested ____ the meeting to Thursday.
note: Never 'suggest to do'. You can also say 'suggest that we move'.

definition: to try not to do something; followed by -ing
example: Try to avoid using too many filler words.
exampleEs: Intenta evitar usar demasiadas muletillas.
cloze: Try to avoid ____ too many filler words.
note: Avoid is always followed by -ing, never by 'to'.

definition: to succeed in doing something difficult
example: We managed to fix the outage before the demo.
exampleEs: Logramos arreglar la caída antes de la demo.
cloze: We managed ____ the outage before the demo.
note: Manage is followed by 'to' + verb, and it suggests the task was hard.

definition: to be excited about something that will happen; 'to' is a preposition
example: I look forward to seeing you at the conference.
exampleEs: Tengo ganas de verte en la conferencia.
cloze: I look forward to ____ you at the conference.
note: The 'to' here is a preposition, so the verb after it takes -ing.

definition: to describe a past habit that no longer continues
example: I used to play every Minecraft update on release day.
exampleEs: Yo solía jugar cada actualización de Minecraft el día de su lanzamiento.
cloze: I used to ____ every Minecraft update on release day.
note: Used to + base verb is for past habits only. It has no present form.

definition: to be familiar with something so it no longer feels strange
example: I'm getting used to having meetings in English.
exampleEs: Me estoy acostumbrando a tener reuniones en inglés.
cloze: I'm getting used to ____ meetings in English.
note: Compare: 'I used to live' (past habit) vs 'I'm used to living' (I'm accustomed). Here 'to' is a preposition.

definition: to end an action that was in progress
example: Please stop interrupting me every five minutes.
exampleEs: Por favor deja de interrumpirme cada cinco minutos.
cloze: Please stop ____ me every five minutes.
note: Stop + -ing means the action ends. Stop + to + verb means you pause in order to do something else.

definition: to pause one activity in order to do another
example: I stopped to review my notes before the call.
exampleEs: Me detuve a revisar mis notas antes de la llamada.
cloze: I stopped ____ my notes before the call.
note: 'I stopped to review' = I paused something else to review. 'I stopped reviewing' = I quit reviewing.

definition: to have a memory of something you did in the past
example: I remember reading about this bug last week.
exampleEs: Recuerdo haber leído sobre este error la semana pasada.
cloze: I remember ____ about this bug last week.
note: Remember + -ing looks backward at a memory. Remember + to looks forward at a duty.

definition: to not forget to do something you need to do
example: Remember to run the build before you merge.
exampleEs: Acuérdate de correr el build antes de hacer el merge.
cloze: Remember ____ the build before you merge.
note: Spanish 'acordarse de' becomes remember + to + verb.

definition: to fail to do something you should have done
example: I forgot to save the file, so nothing was kept.
exampleEs: Olvidé guardar el archivo, así que no se conservó nada.
cloze: I forgot ____ the file, so nothing was kept.
note: Forget + to = you didn't do it. Forget + -ing = you did it but have no memory of it.

es: ayudar a alguien a hacer algo
definition: to make it easier for someone to do something
example: This tool helps developers find bugs faster.
exampleEs: Esta herramienta ayuda a los desarrolladores a encontrar errores más rápido.
cloze: This tool helps developers ____ bugs faster.
note: Help can be followed by the bare verb or 'to': 'help me find' = 'help me to find'.

definition: to get pleasure from an activity; followed by -ing
example: I enjoy testing new AI tools on weekends.
exampleEs: Disfruto probar nuevas herramientas de IA los fines de semana.
cloze: I enjoy ____ new AI tools on weekends.
note: Enjoy is never followed by 'to + verb'.

definition: to make a choice to do something
example: We decided to migrate the project to Postgres.
exampleEs: Decidimos migrar el proyecto a Postgres.
cloze: We decided ____ the project to Postgres.
note: Decide takes 'to' + verb. Use 'decide on' with a noun: 'decide on a name'.

definition: to want and expect something to happen
example: I hope to reach B2 by March.
exampleEs: Espero llegar a B2 para marzo.
cloze: I hope ____ B2 by March.
note: 'Hope' is not 'esperar' when you mean wait. To wait for something, use 'wait for'.

definition: to have an intention to do something
example: We plan to ship the feature next sprint.
exampleEs: Planeamos lanzar la función en el próximo sprint.
cloze: We plan ____ the feature next sprint.
note: Plan + to + verb. With a noun use 'plan for': 'plan for the launch'.

definition: to say you will definitely do something
example: He promised to send the report by noon.
exampleEs: Prometió enviar el informe antes del mediodía.
cloze: He promised ____ the report by noon.
note: Promise + to + verb, not 'promise that + infinitive'.

definition: to say you will not do something
example: The server refuses to accept the request.
exampleEs: El servidor se niega a aceptar la solicitud.
cloze: The server refuses ____ the request.
note: Do not confuse refuse (negarse) with 'reject' (rechazar a algo).

definition: to say yes to doing something
example: They agreed to extend the deadline.
exampleEs: Aceptaron extender la fecha límite.
cloze: They agreed ____ the deadline.
note: Agree + to + verb. Agree with a person; agree on a topic.

definition: to say you are willing to do something for someone
example: She offered to help me prepare for the demo.
exampleEs: Se ofreció a ayudarme a preparar la demo.
cloze: She offered ____ me prepare for the demo.
note: Offer + to + verb means 'volunteer to'. Do not say 'offered me to help'.

definition: a polite way to say what you want someone to do
example: I'd like you to review the slides before the call.
exampleEs: Me gustaría que revisaras las diapositivas antes de la llamada.
cloze: I'd like you ____ the slides before the call.
note: Like want, it needs object + to. 'I'd like that you review' is a common Spanish-speaker error.

es: pedirle a alguien que haga algo
definition: to request that someone do something
example: Could you ask the team to check the logs?
exampleEs: ¿Podrías pedirle al equipo que revise los registros?
cloze: Could you ask the team ____ the logs?
note: Ask + person + to + verb. Do not use 'ask that' with a subjunctive.

es: decirle a alguien que haga algo
definition: to give someone an instruction
example: The lead told us to rehearse the demo twice.
exampleEs: El líder nos dijo que ensayáramos la demo dos veces.
cloze: The lead told us ____ the demo twice.
note: Tell needs a person right after it: 'told us to', never 'told to'.

definition: to give permission for someone to do something
example: The settings allow users to create their own server rules.
exampleEs: La configuración permite que los usuarios creen sus propias reglas de servidor.
cloze: The settings allow users ____ their own server rules.
note: Allow + person + to. You can say 'allow editing' with no person, but 'allow to edit' is wrong.

es: aconsejar a alguien que haga algo
definition: to recommend a course of action to someone
example: The doctor advised him to sleep more.
exampleEs: El doctor le aconsejó dormir más.
cloze: The doctor advised him ____ more.
note: The noun is 'advice' (uncountable); the verb is 'advise'. Advise + person + to + verb.

es: animar a alguien a hacer algo
definition: to give someone confidence or support to do something
example: Our mentor encourages us to ask questions.
exampleEs: Nuestro mentor nos anima a hacer preguntas.
cloze: Our mentor encourages us ____ questions.
note: Encourage + person + to + verb.

definition: to believe or require that someone will do something
example: They expect me to present the update in English.
exampleEs: Esperan que yo presente la actualización en inglés.
cloze: They expect me ____ the update in English.
note: Spanish 'esperar que + subjunctive' becomes expect + person + to.

definition: to make something necessary for someone
example: The rules require members to verify their account.
exampleEs: Las reglas exigen que los miembros verifiquen su cuenta.
cloze: The rules require members ____ their account.
note: Require sounds more formal than 'need'. Require + person + to + verb.

definition: to say that something is a good idea; followed by -ing
example: I recommend clearing the cache before testing.
exampleEs: Recomiendo borrar la caché antes de probar.
cloze: I recommend ____ the cache before testing.
note: Do not say 'recommend to do'. Use 'recommend doing' or 'recommend that you do'.

definition: to be bothered by something; used in polite requests
example: Do you mind closing the window?
exampleEs: ¿Te molesta cerrar la ventana?
cloze: Do you mind ____ the window?
note: 'Do you mind...?' means 'is it a problem?'. Answer 'No, not at all' to agree politely.

definition: to complete an activity; followed by -ing
example: Let's finish writing the docs first.
exampleEs: Terminemos de escribir la documentación primero.
cloze: Let's finish ____ the docs first.
note: Finish is followed by -ing, never by 'to'.

definition: to continue doing something, often repeatedly
example: Keep trying until the tests pass.
exampleEs: Sigue intentando hasta que las pruebas pasen.
cloze: Keep ____ until the tests pass.
note: Keep + -ing = continue. 'Keep on trying' is also correct.

definition: to repeat an activity to improve at it
example: I practice giving my pitch every morning.
exampleEs: Practico dar mi pitch cada mañana.
cloze: I practice ____ my pitch every morning.
note: Practice is followed by -ing. In US English the verb is spelled 'practice' too.

definition: to think carefully about doing something
example: We're considering switching to a new vendor.
exampleEs: Estamos considerando cambiar a un nuevo proveedor.
cloze: We're considering ____ to a new vendor.
note: Consider + -ing. It does not take 'to + verb'.

definition: to say that you did something wrong
example: He admitted deleting the wrong file.
exampleEs: Admitió haber borrado el archivo equivocado.
cloze: He admitted ____ the wrong file.
note: Admit + -ing refers to a past action.

definition: to say that you did not do something
example: She denied sending the message.
exampleEs: Negó haber enviado el mensaje.
cloze: She denied ____ the message.
note: Deny + -ing. Do not confuse with 'refuse to' (negarse a).

definition: to do something that could have a bad result
example: Don't risk losing your account by using shady bots.
exampleEs: No arriesgues perder tu cuenta usando bots sospechosos.
cloze: Don't risk ____ your account by using shady bots.
note: Risk is followed by -ing.

definition: to form a picture of something in your mind
example: Imagine building a whole Minecraft server from one prompt.
exampleEs: Imagina construir un servidor entero de Minecraft con un solo prompt.
cloze: Imagine ____ a whole Minecraft server from one prompt.
note: Imagine + -ing.

definition: to be unable to stop yourself from doing something
example: I can't help smiling when I see a clean codebase.
exampleEs: No puedo evitar sonreír cuando veo un código limpio.
cloze: I can't help ____ when I see a clean codebase.
note: Can't help + -ing is an involuntary reaction. 'Can't help you' is different: it means 'unable to assist'.

definition: to be good enough to deserve the effort
example: It's worth reading the docs before asking.
exampleEs: Vale la pena leer la documentación antes de preguntar.
cloze: It's worth ____ the docs before asking.
note: Worth is followed by -ing, not by an infinitive.

es: estar a punto de hacer algo
definition: to be going to do something very soon
example: Sorry, the call is about to start, so I have to go.
exampleEs: Perdón, la llamada está a punto de empezar, así que me tengo que ir.
cloze: Sorry, the call is about ____, so I have to go.
note: Be about + to + verb. Do not use 'about to' with -ing.

definition: to not succeed in doing something
example: The script failed to load the config file.
exampleEs: El script no logró cargar el archivo de configuración.
cloze: The script failed ____ the config file.
note: Fail + to + verb often appears in error messages and reports.

definition: to give the impression of doing or being something
example: The model seems to lose context after long chats.
exampleEs: El modelo parece perder contexto después de chats largos.
cloze: The model seems ____ context after long chats.
note: Seem + to + verb. 'It seems that...' is another option.

definition: to usually or often do something
example: I tend to rush when I'm nervous.
exampleEs: Tiendo a apresurarme cuando estoy nervioso.
cloze: I tend ____ when I'm nervous.
note: Tend + to + verb, not 'tend to be like very...' (use an adverb instead).

definition: to have enough money or time to do something
example: We can't afford to lose another week.
exampleEs: No podemos permitirnos perder otra semana.
cloze: We can't afford ____ another week.
note: Afford is normally used with can/could and followed by 'to'.

definition: to like one activity more than another
example: I prefer speaking in English, even if I make mistakes.
exampleEs: Prefiero hablar en inglés, aunque cometa errores.
cloze: I prefer ____ in English, even if I make mistakes.
note: Prefer doing X to doing Y. 'Prefer to do' is also correct for a specific occasion.

definition: to express a preference; followed by the bare verb
example: I'd rather call than read a long email.
exampleEs: Prefiero llamar que leer un correo largo.
cloze: I'd rather ____ than read a long email.
note: Would rather + base verb, with no 'to'. Negative: 'I'd rather not go'.

es: se supone que uno debe hacer algo
definition: to be expected or required to do something
example: We're supposed to submit the report today.
exampleEs: Se supone que debemos entregar el informe hoy.
cloze: We're supposed ____ the report today.
note: Always 'supposed' with a final -d, followed by 'to'.

definition: to have permission to do something
example: Interns aren't allowed to access production.
exampleEs: A los practicantes no se les permite acceder a producción.
cloze: Interns aren't allowed ____ production.
note: The passive form of allow. Active: 'They don't allow interns to access it'.

definition: to demand strongly to do something
example: She insisted on testing the code herself.
exampleEs: Insistió en probar el código ella misma.
cloze: She insisted on ____ the code herself.
note: Insist is followed by 'on' + -ing. Do not say 'insist to do'.

definition: to achieve something you were trying to do
example: We succeeded in reducing latency by 40%.
exampleEs: Logramos reducir la latencia en un 40%.
cloze: We succeeded in ____ latency by 40%.
note: Succeed in + -ing. 'Success' is a noun; 'succeed' is not 'suceder' (to happen).

definition: to say sorry for something you did
example: I apologize for being late.
exampleEs: Me disculpo por llegar tarde.
cloze: I apologize for ____ late.
note: Apologize for + -ing or noun. Never 'apologize to be late'.

definition: to want to do or learn about something
example: I'm interested in starting a startup.
exampleEs: Estoy interesado en iniciar una startup.
cloze: I'm interested in ____ a startup.
note: Interested in + -ing. The preposition is 'in', not 'on' or 'by'.

definition: to stop someone from doing something
example: A firewall prevents attackers from getting in.
exampleEs: Un firewall impide que los atacantes entren.
cloze: A firewall prevents attackers from ____ in.
note: Prevent + person + from + -ing. 'From' is required.

es: agradecer a alguien por hacer algo
definition: to express gratitude for something someone did
example: Thanks for helping me with the slides.
exampleEs: Gracias por ayudarme con las diapositivas.
cloze: Thanks for ____ me with the slides.
note: Thank for + -ing, not 'thanks to help me'.

definition: to use time on an activity
example: I spend hours experimenting with prompts.
exampleEs: Paso horas experimentando con prompts.
cloze: I spend hours ____ with prompts.
note: Spend time + -ing, with no 'in' or 'to'.

definition: to find something difficult to do
example: I have trouble finding the right word when I speak.
exampleEs: Me cuesta encontrar la palabra correcta cuando hablo.
cloze: I have trouble ____ the right word when I speak.
note: Have trouble + -ing, with no preposition.
